newsitem.title: USA: Equitable's DLJ, Alliance aid results.
newsitem.headline: Equitable's DLJ, Alliance aid results.

text.p: The Equitable Cos Inc said its Donaldson Lufkin & Jennrette and Alliance Capital units contributed a combined $248.6 million in 1996 to Equitable's profits, up 31 percent from the $217.6 million reported in 1995.
Results at Equitable's DLJ were helped by higher underwriting commissions and fees, as well as stronger results at its Pershing division.

Mutual fund mania helped Alliance Capital's results as the number of assets under management swelled 25 percent to $182.8 billion in 1996 with the help of new money inflows and appreciation, Equitable said.
DLJ's after-tax operating earnings rose to a record $291.3 million for 1996, 58 percent above the $183.8 million the previous year.
For 1996, Alliance's after-tax operating earnings -- before minority interests and other expenses -- grew 24 percent to $193.4 million, compared with $155.4 million for 1995.
DLJ and Alliance Capital are both publicly traded units of Equitable. Equitable is a U.S. majority-owned subsidiary of French insurance and banking group AXA SA.
